item.title: Trump approves disaster assistance to DC to help with sewage spill into Potomac River
item.description: President Donald Trump has approved emergency assistance to Washington, D.C., to help the city address a sewage system leak that dumped at least 250 million gallons of raw sewage into the Potomac River. The Federal Emergency Management Agency announced Trump’s approval on Saturday, allowing FEMA to provide equipment and resources to help with the response to the Jan. 19 spill after a pipeline ruptured. item.title: NYC nursing walkout ends as last striking nurses approve new contract
item.description: Thousands of nurses at a major New York hospital system have approved a new contract, voting to end a strike after more than a month. The nurses’ union announced the vote results Saturday. More than 4,000 nurses in the privately run NewYork-Presbyterian system have been on strike since Jan. 12. They are now due to start returning to work in the coming week. The union, called the New York State Nurses Association, and the hospital system said Friday that they had reached a tentative deal. item.title: Bridgeman delivers brilliant performance at Riviera to build a 6-shot lead over McIlroy
item.description: Jacob Bridgeman is turning the Genesis Invitational at Riviera into a runaway. He started the third round in a share of the lead. item.title: No. 4 Arizona steadies the ship with a gritty 73-66 win at No. 2 Houston
item.description: Arizona wasn’t feeling great after losing consecutive games following a 23-0 start. “The two losses just didn’t taste right in the mouth,” Arizona’s Ivan Kharchenko said. The fourth-ranked Wildcats are feeling a lot better now after winning two straight following that skid, capped by Saturday’s 73-66 victory over No. 2 Houston that gave them sole possession of first place in the Big 12 Conference. item.description: The WNBA sent a counterproposal to its players’ union for a new collective bargaining agreement that included continuing to pay for all player housing this season, but not really changing its previous offer of revenue sharing. item.title: A long-acting HIV drug arrives in Zimbabwe for some at highest risk
item.description: Zimbabwe is one of the world's first countries to roll out lenacapavir, a long-acting HIV prevention drug that is administered only twice a year. It offers new hope for high-risk groups struggling with adherence to daily prevention pills. Early recipients, including sex workers, say the injectable drug reduces stigma and improves convenience.
